title: Self-sufficiency or fatigue – scenarios to bookend European defence spending outlook
gist: Oxford Economics models two bookend scenarios for European defence spending - a rapid self-sufficiency push versus a fatigue-driven pullback - finding both leave medium-term GDP nearly unchanged (±0.1-0.2pp) but diverge sharply on fiscal cost, with self-sufficiency pushing peripheral bond yields up 40-50bp.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics models two scenarios bookending the EU's defence spending outlook: a rapid push for defence self-sufficiency and a pullback driven by spending fatigue.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Gives investors two bounding cases to size European fiscal and bond-market risk from defence spending rather than a single point forecast.
insights.quote: We model two scenarios to bookend this uncertainty: a rapid drive for defence self-sufficiency, and a scenario where spending fatigue sets in.
insights.locator: The EU's defence spending ramp-up carries real consequences

insights.claim: Neither of the two European defence-spending scenarios moves medium-term Eurozone GDP dramatically - growth ends up only 0.1-0.2 percentage points higher or lower over the next three years.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: The growth impact of European defence spending swings is second-order; it should not be a primary driver of Eurozone GDP forecasts or equity allocation.
insights.quote: growth ends up 0.1-0.2 percentage points higher or lower over the next three years
insights.locator: The EU's defence spending ramp-up carries real consequences

insights.claim: The self-sufficiency scenario puts considerably more strain on Europe's public finances than the fatigue scenario, even though both produce similarly modest GDP effects.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Fiscal and bond-market risk, not growth, is the key differentiator between the two paths - investors should watch sovereign spreads more than GDP prints.
insights.quote: the self-sufficiency path puts considerably more strain on Europe's public finances.
insights.locator: The EU's defence spending ramp-up carries real consequences

insights.claim: In the self-sufficiency scenario, European NATO countries must close a €1 trillion gap in equipment and personnel to reduce reliance on the US, which is €400bn more than Oxford Economics' baseline already assumes.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Sizes incremental European defence procurement demand well above current baseline forecasts, relevant for defence-sector revenue and government issuance modeling.
insights.quote: European NATO countries need to close a €1tn gap in equipment and personnel to reduce reliance on the US – €400bn more than our baseline already assumes.
insights.locator: In the self-sufficiency scenario, European NATO countries need to close

insights.claim: Despite the scale of the self-sufficiency spending push, the boost to GDP is modest and front-loaded because defence fiscal multipliers are low and the urgency of the ramp-up pushes more spending into imports rather than domestic output.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Investors shouldn't expect a large domestic growth dividend from higher European defence budgets; import-heavy procurement caps the upside for local industrial output.
insights.quote: defence multipliers are low and the need for speed pushes more of the spending into imports
insights.locator: Despite the scale of this spending, the lift to GDP

insights.claim: Under the self-sufficiency scenario, long-term bond yields rise by 40-50 basis points in the most fiscally stretched European countries, including Italy and Spain, though EU-level funding could help cap that increase.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Flags Italian and Spanish sovereign bonds as the assets most exposed to a self-sufficiency-driven fiscal push, with joint EU financing as a mitigant to watch for.
insights.quote: long-term bond yields rise by 40-50 basis points in the most fiscally stretched countries, including Italy and Spain, though EU-level funding could help cap the increase.

insights.claim: An end to the Russia-Ukraine war combined with a wave of European elections could push defence spending down governments' priority lists, driving the fatigue scenario.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: A peace deal or election-cycle shift are the political catalysts to monitor for a European defence-spending pullback trade.
insights.quote: An end to the Russia-Ukraine war and a wave of European elections could push defence spending down governments' priority lists
insights.locator: The fatigue scenario paints a different picture.

insights.claim: In the fatigue scenario, weaker public backing could prompt some European countries to cut defence expenditure by 0.5-1% of GDP by 2028.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Sizes the downside risk to European defence order books and government bond issuance plans if political appetite for spending fades.
insights.quote: weaker public backing prompting some countries to cut expenditure by 0.5-1% of GDP by 2028
insights.locator: The fatigue scenario paints a different picture.

insights.claim: The fatigue scenario's spending cuts would shave around 0.2 percentage points off Eurozone growth over the next two years.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Quantifies the growth drag investors should model into Eurozone GDP forecasts if the fatigue scenario materializes.
insights.quote: This would shave around 0.2 percentage points off Eurozone growth over the next two years
insights.locator: The fatigue scenario paints a different picture.

insights.claim: In the fatigue scenario, the sharpest defence-spending pullback would occur in southern European countries furthest from Russia.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Identifies southern Europe as the country group most likely to under-deliver on defence commitments - a signal for country-level fiscal and political risk assessment.
insights.quote: with the sharpest pullback in southern European countries furthest from Russia.
insights.locator: The fatigue scenario paints a different picture.
